data.title: Signing custody: persist wire-minted keys and links through LocalKeystore; OutcomeUnknown at protocol 3.9 (re-review after cr-1dc5ii)

data.body:
[HIGH] Attacker-controlled ancestor symlink can retarget the keystore after validation. check_dir records both written and resolved ancestors, but it skips owner and mode checks for every written symlink here. Later operations resolve store.dir again: acquire builds the lock path at lines 1319-1320, open builds state and key paths at lines 1445 and 1460, and replace_state builds paths at lines 1671-1675 then renames at line 1703. No directory descriptor or inode binding connects those operations to the directory that passed validation. An attacker who owns a symlink under a sticky shared parent can switch it between two otherwise valid stores. O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final path component. This can load a different signing key or state, or lock one store while mutating another.

Failure modes: signer or custody-state substitution; lock and mutation against different stores; concurrent-writer protection bypass; fail-closed availability loss.
Edge cases: sticky shared directories such as /tmp; two valid victim-owned stores; a synchronized retarget after canonicalize; final-component O_NOFOLLOW does not cover ancestor symlinks.
Rollback: reject any untrusted ancestor symlink as a minimum containment. The robust fix must walk ancestors without following links, retain a trusted store-directory descriptor, and perform lock, key, state, temporary-file, and rename operations relative to that descriptor. Keep the separate risk:critical human gate.
Monitoring: count typed untrusted-ancestor and directory-identity mismatch refusals without logging secret or sensitive path data. Detect store inode changes before each custody operation.
Validation: add a deterministic barrier after directory validation. Retarget an attacker-owned ancestor symlink, then prove open, load, persist, and sweep all refuse and never touch the alternate store. Also prove lock and state operations use the same directory inode. Do not use sleeps.

data.reason: [HIGH] crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1236-1241 skips trust checks for written ancestor symlinks, while later lock, open, and rename operations resolve the mutable pathname again. An attacker can retarget custody between valid stores after validation. See thread th-c57e6q.

data.body: [FIXED] The target now walks every resolved component, checks symlink ownership, pins the store directory device and inode, and rechecks before sensitive operations. The deterministic swap test covers the original retarget window. A separate hard-linked-symlink bypass remains and is recorded in a new thread.

data.reason: Original ancestor-symlink retarget race is fixed at target 343f992109b6288f3611523d6963f6c513865f09; separate hard-link bypass remains.

data.body:
[HIGH] The owner check accepts a hard-linked symlink as trusted. Linux permits another local user to hard-link a victim-owned symlink when fs.protected_hardlinks is disabled. The new walk then sees the victim uid here and follows the link. The module documents this at lines 69-71, but the runtime neither rejects ancestor symlinks nor verifies the kernel protection. An attacker with write access to a sticky shared parent can place an owner-attributed link at a missing path component and redirect startup to another owner-controlled keystore. That substitutes the signing identity despite the local-user boundary at lines 45-46.

Failure modes: wrong signing key and custody state load; lock acquisition on the wrong store; persistent signing under an attacker-selected owner-owned store; fail-closed availability loss.
Edge cases: fs.protected_hardlinks=0; platforms without that Linux control; a hard-linked absolute symlink to another valid store; a relative symlink whose meaning changes at the attacker-selected destination.
Rollback: restore the prior rejection of ancestor symlinks, or use descriptor-relative traversal that binds each component. If owner symlinks remain supported, fail closed unless the platform proves hard-link protection for symlinks. Keep the separate risk:critical human gate.
Monitoring: count typed ancestor-symlink and unsupported-hardlink-policy refusals without logging sensitive paths. Record directory identity mismatches separately.
Validation: under a disposable mount namespace with protected_hardlinks disabled, create a victim-owned symlink, hard-link it into a sticky shared parent as another uid, and prove open, load, persist, sweep, and lock all refuse without touching either store. Add a supported-platform control and avoid sleeps.

data.reason: [HIGH] crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1302-1303 trusts symlink inode ownership, so a hard-linked victim symlink can bypass the local-user ancestry boundary when protected hardlinks are unavailable or disabled.

data.body: [FIXED] The current target closes this HIGH path. `trusted_symlink` rejects every traversed symlink whose holder has group or other write bits at crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1294-1301. It then enforces the owner rule and rejects link count other than one at crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1302-1307. `check_dir` also requires the store directory to have no group or other permissions at crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1422-1430. Failure modes: key or state substitution, cross-store locking, and signing under an attacker-selected store now fail closed. Edge cases: sticky shared parents, protected_hardlinks disabled, absolute and relative symlinks, and pre-existing extra links are refused. Rollback: removing the new holder, link-count, or private-directory checks reopens the original attack, so retain all three controls. Monitoring: LinkedAncestor, UnsafeParent, and StoreMoved remain typed refusals without secret content. Validation: crates/continuum-security/tests/keystore.rs:1113-1173 covers writable and sticky holders, lines 1202-1268 covers deterministic retargeting, and lines 1311-1335 covers the hard-linked symlink. The separate risk:critical human gate remains required.

data.reason: The target rejects writable symlink holders, multi-link symlinks, and non-private store directories.

Reviewed the full persisted range 6a16ad22a5a70e382c7fad11f3a9c389a8cf98ca..4812c023aa2fd125cf9aae234b7f6466f1b0107c at the exact target. No unresolved security findings remain. The prior HIGH hard-linked symlink path is fixed by writable-holder rejection, single-link enforcement, and private store-directory checks. Failure modes now fail closed. Sticky-directory and disabled protected_hardlinks edge cases are covered. Rollback must retain all three controls. Typed refusals provide monitoring. Deterministic retarget and hard-link tests provide validation. This LGTM does not satisfy the separate risk:critical human approval gate.
